All product gates remain unrun. Local acceptance of a relationship is distinct from protocol WorkApproval.
Exact Coop source licensing, model compatibility and commons draft mappings remain implementation prerequisites.
KOI partial-node architecture selected for planning: browser-owned history and inference, optional controlled full node, explicit sharing and scoped reconciliation.
User authorized updating draft PR #1073; K1/K2 and E9–E11 remain unrun. No production peer, dependency installation or runtime implementation is authorized by this plan revision.

Published portable public-safe HTML design studies and a next-session handoff. Private-note-derived fixtures were replaced with synthetic records; no runtime, dependency or product gate is complete.

2026-10-23: prototype specification added (prototype.md): Gemma, KOI, Pi Durable and WebMCP in one demo loop, slices G0 to G4, ten decisions and six demo checks; connects through the public garden page's WebMCP tool and uses Pi Durable 1.4.0 IndexedDbStorage. No implementation started.

2026-10-24: the prototype's four open questions were decided (public garden page first; Brave Beta with the WebMCP flag, Chrome only as fallback; Grove works without WebMCP through a direct adapter and an externally_connectable API; TAS second; counts toward A0 to A4). G0 authorized as a disposable spike in its own session; hub not promoted; nothing built.

2026-10-24: correction: the connection surface is the Admin Hub, not the public garden page (prototype decisions 18 to 21): a read-only garden snapshot tool behind a Hub setting, protocol records with approval state, direct Shared readers without WebMCP; the client's own navigator.modelContext fix ships separately.

2026-10-24: design direction agreed (prototype decisions 22 to 25, prototype-design.md): Grove is a third Warm Earth dialect on the cockpit's dials with the garden tone, an ink-and-stone canvas legend, and Storybook Design System pages as proof.

2026-11-13: user accepted capture → review → share for knowledge and impact evidence. Local community identity is independent of chain/address; encrypted sharing excludes hosting operators. community-sharing.md is the current contract, with architecture-flows.md and sharing-research.md.

2026-11-13: Solid is the first optional hosted-storage adapter, not identity/key authority. ATProto/Certified, Ethereum, KOI and archive connections are optional. Yjs/MLS are conditional; offline encrypted bundles and paired-device networking precede generalized mesh.

2026-11-13: C0–C6 and E15–E21 added, all unrun. Historical G0 synthetic desktop report exists but does not pass private-sharing, phone or persistent Pi tab-close gates. Earlier S/P/K IDs and lane states preserved. Planning-only revision; no runtime/dependency or external Linear changes.

2026-11-13 follow-up: C1a/E22 define a planned, unrun two-device Solid-versus-EDV comparison with local keys, recovery, scoped roles, host privacy and build burden. E23 and identity-role-mapping.md separate community/member associations and current protocol roles from proposed local grants. local-first-options.md shortlists candidates; Pi source refresh records 1.5.2 manifest and deferred-progress limits, without changing installed versions. Lanes/Linear metadata remain unchanged; no backend selected by this plan revision.

2026-11-13 accepted follow-up: C0a/E24 plan existing-passkey reuse, actual PRF support, offline unlock and independent recovery on phone/laptop. C5/E25 now compare Yjs with Automerge + Keyhive using the same synthetic two-device fixture, scoped permissions, host privacy, revocation, history and engine-state recovery. Keyhive remains experimental; Solid/EDVs remain optional and a tested ciphertext relay may serve the slice without either. collaboration-passkey-spike.md owns the experiment. All product gates remain unrun; lane and Linear metadata preserved; no dependency/runtime/account changes.

2026-11-13 accepted preferences: Solid is the preferred optional hosted-storage adapter with client-side encryption; Yjs is preferred for optional co-editing with verified writer permissions. Community/member identity and private keys remain local. EDV and Automerge + Keyhive remain research alternatives, Keyhive experimental and synthetic-data-only. Encrypted record exchange stays the baseline. C1a/C3/E18/E22 validate Solid first; C5/E20 gates optional Yjs, while E25 alternative research is independent. No implementation, installation or completed runtime gate; lane and Linear metadata preserved.

2026-11-13: user authorized commit and push of Grove plan/visual updates. Added the synthetic standalone architecture page and editable fragment under artifacts/demos. Publication preparation only; result/commit/gate evidence to be reported after execution. No implementation gate, lane or Linear state advanced.

2026-11-14: two independent reviewers examined the architecture and MVP (one on product, flows and scope; one on identity, encryption and synchronization), and their findings were reconciled. spec.md now owns the MVP contract and the single decision log: D1–D25, recommendations R1–R15, assumptions W1–W4 and open questions O1–O11.

2026-11-14 owner decisions: the desktop extension and a phone web app ship together; the author approves every share of their own capture and a steward approves partner summaries and public releases; one steward signs member changes, with a recovery code at setup and a second controller before real data; the existing passkey unlocks the vault where its provider supports it and a passphrase does otherwise, so C0a is a gate; the graph, Gemma and Pi stay in the MVP; the no-decrypt requirement covers storage and relay hosts, with Green Goods trusted as publisher of the client code.

2026-11-14 owner decisions, continued: encrypted files carry records in the MVP and a hosted mailbox with Solid preferred is the next lane; the MVP graph shows Grove's own records, with the Hub snapshot and KOI exchange as next lanes; community is Grove's term, defined apart from a Garden and the Community role; a device stops sharing when its member list is older than seven days, adjustable per community. The earlier note that the living graph is the core interface is superseded: the graph is one view beside capture and review lists.

2026-11-14: C0b/E26 added (device durability, run first). MVP order: C0b, C0a, C1, C0, recovery, C2, C4, with the workspace lane (S1–S6, S8, P0–P2) alongside. Open with the owner: where the phone app and shared core live (O2) and whether Coop code may be reused (O5). The architecture page was rebuilt as one self-contained file. All gates remain unrun; no lane, Linear, dependency or runtime change; the documentation edits are uncommitted in a review worktree.

2026-11-14 owner decisions on the agent (D26–D30): it captures relevant knowledge and resources as a person uses their browser and brings them in for that person to review and then share; it may read every page visited except private windows and a block list of sensitive sites; a person reviews everything it brings in and can discard it, and it never brings in an item it would recommend discarding; its assessment first covers why an item was brought in, its source, author and date, and whether it is safe to share; the steward writes the community's focus in Grove. S13–S15 and E27–E28 added to the workspace lane, unrun. Passive capture is therefore in the MVP, replacing the earlier selected-domain research session.

2026-11-14 framing corrected by the owner (D31–D36): the project makes Green Goods work in a fully local environment with a phone, a browser and an extension, and all current functionality works there in essence; Grove is the extension only, adding knowledge capture and agentic flows; locally a community is its Garden, which supersedes D23; work and promises can be reported free-form or through the existing screens; an agent structures a free-form report at any review on a laptop, into the existing report contract and promise fields. Added S16, E29, a first function table and open questions O14–O18. The plan has not been reworked function by function. All gates remain unrun; no lane, Linear, dependency or runtime change.

2026-11-14 owner answers that shape the plan (D37–D44): the gardener app and the steward cockpit gain local operation together; a new garden starts fully locally and an existing one is brought local with one connected read; the plan follows the Green Goods chain (Actions and assessment, work, approval, report), then promises, joining and roles, and money and certificates; money is recorded now and settled when connected; Grove works beside the app's screens through a bridge; carried files first, then direct sync between open devices; the garden's assessment is the agent's focus; local operation lives in separate local builds. Added C7–C10, F1–F7 and E30–E38, all unrun. Resolved O2, O14 and O15. The owner also decided that a steward alone may include an approved work report in a report to a funder (D45). No lane, Linear, dependency or runtime change.

2026-11-14 owner decision on where the local builds are developed (D46): at alpha.greengoods.app for the app and alpha.admin.greengoods.app for the cockpit, new subdomains of greengoods.app, and not in the beta environment. Whether real gardens first install from those addresses is confirmed before a pilot with real data (O2). No lane, Linear, dependency or runtime change.

2026-11-14 owner decisions from review: an imported garden records its local identifier onchain, so a second steward finds it and joins instead of making a copy (D47); and running a pool's seasons, support allocations and editing an Action are in the first version (D37). No lane, Linear, dependency or runtime change.

2026-11-14 owner decisions, evening: each function block starts with an inventory of every action its screens and contracts offer today, and its gate covers that list (D48); a free-form report can be a voice note with photos and documents, which the local agent transcribes and structures on a laptop into one record or several, and only a structured record can be approved (D49, amending D34–D36). No lane, Linear, dependency or runtime change.

2026-11-14 owner decisions, late evening: from a voice note the agent also proposes knowledge, such as a lesson or the questions people asked (D50); an owner of the garden can replace an imported garden's onchain record, so a first importer who pairs nobody cannot lock the garden out (D51); and leaving a current function out of the first version takes the owner's recorded decision, without which its gate does not pass (D48). No lane, Linear, dependency or runtime change.

Owner decisions, 14 November (15 November UTC): when an owner replaces an imported garden's onchain record the garden is carried over, with the owner's device as signer and its members, roles and records as they were (D52); and a device the steward adds for a member who has lost every device and their recovery code approves sharing only for records made after it was added (D53). No lane, Linear, dependency or runtime change.

Owner's observation, 14 November (15 November UTC): work, approvals and promises now happen offline first, so an attestation's time would be when a record was brought onchain, not when the work or promise was done or approved. Recorded as open question O20, with what today's Work and WorkApproval resolvers do with that time. No decision, lane, Linear, dependency or runtime change.

Owner decisions, 14 November (15 November UTC): a time-based rule uses when the work happened, as the report says, so work done inside an Action's window counts even when it is reported, approved or brought onchain after it (D54); and the record of a local garden's identifier lives in one new attestation schema with no resolver, checked on devices (D55, C11). O20 is resolved in part. No lane, Linear, dependency or runtime change; registering the schema needs its own go-ahead.
